nodes.name: Fast thermal treatment of Ni-MOFs
nodes.procedure: Hydroxyl-rich Ni/Ni₃C nanoparticles (OH-Ni/Ni₃C) encapsulated in a carbon matrix were synthesized by a fast-thermal treatment approach from a Ni-MOFs precursor with H₂ as the reductive agent. During the process, the atomically dispersed Ni sites were reduced rapidly to elemental Ni, accompanied by the interstitial doping of the light element of carbon. The phase transform will bring about abundant vacancies and lattice mismatch, and then, the anchoring of -OH groups on the interface to stabilize the high-energy surface. The morphology of Ni-MOFs was preserved as the carbon matrix to anchor OH-Ni/Ni₃C nanoparticles with an average size of around 15 nm.
nodes.source_text: Hydroxyl-rich Ni/Ni₃C nanoparticles (OH-Ni/Ni₃C) encapsulated in a carbon matrix were synthesized by a fast-thermal treatment approach from a Ni-MOFs precursor with H₂ as the reductive agent (Figure 1a, Supporting Information Figure S1).

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM shows the morphology of Ni-MOFs was preserved as the carbon matrix to anchor OH-Ni/Ni₃C nanoparticles.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM) patterns showed the morphology of Ni-MOFs was preserved as the carbon matrix to anchor OH-Ni/Ni₃C nanoparticles with an average size of around 15 nm (Figure 1b, c, Supporting Information Figure S2).

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows OH-Ni/Ni₃C nanoparticles with average size of around 15 nm and abundant stacking faults and vacancies on the surface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM) patterns showed the morphology of Ni-MOFs was preserved as the carbon matrix to anchor OH-Ni/Ni₃C nanoparticles with an average size of around 15 nm (Figure 1b, c, Supporting Information Figure S2). Intuitively, HRTEM images displayed abundant stacking faults and vacancies on the OH-Ni/Ni₃C surface (Supporting Information Figure S3).

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM shows distinct phase interface of OH-Ni/Ni₃C with interplanar distances of 0.179 nm (200) facets of cubic Ni and 0.215 nm (006) facets of hexagonal Ni₃C.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-angle annular dark-field scanning TEM (HAADF-STEM) image in Figure 1d demonstrated a visually distinct phase interface. The extracted interplanar distances of 0.179 nm and 0.215 nm can be indexed to the specific crystals of (200) facets of cubic Ni and (006) facets of hexagonal Ni₃C, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS mappings show uneven distribution of C in the region of Ni and O element limited to the core of Ni/Ni₃C nanoparticles.
nodes.evidence_snippet: This conclusion was further supported by the uneven distribution of C in the region of Ni in the energy-dispersive spectroscopy (EDS) mappings. As expected, the O element was observable and limited to the core of Ni/Ni₃C nanoparticles, implying the anchoring of -OH groups.

nodes.characterization_summary: High-resolution XPS confirms Ni phases and Niᴵᴵ-OH at 855.8 eV in Ni 2p₃/₂ for OH-Ni/Ni₃C, with decreased Ni-OH intensity in O 1s for Ni/Ni₃C compared to OH-Ni/Ni₃C and OH-Ni.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 1f, the maxima peak at 852.5 eV in Ni2p₃/₂ spectra corresponded to the prime phase of metal Ni.[6b] The Niᴵ peak of Ni₃C was located at 853.5 eV... an obvious peak signal collected at the higher binding energy of 855.8 eV could be assignable to Niᴵᴵ-OH... The Niᴵᴵ-OH was further characterized by the O 1s core-level spectra (Figure 1g). As expected, Ni/Ni₃C represented a significantly decreased intensity of Ni-OH peak after extra thermal treatment in inert Ar...

nodes.characterization_summary: Temperature-dependent ATR-FTIR shows terminal M-OH and bridging [O²⁻]-H groups observable even at 250°C for OH-Ni/Ni₃C.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The temperature-dependent attenuated total reflection (ATR) FTIR spectra of OH-Ni/Ni₃C are shown in Figure 1h. The two distinct peaks attributable to terminal M-OH and bridging [O²⁻]-H groups were clearly observable even at the high temperature of 250°C, demonstrating a strong interaction between -OH groups and Ni/Ni₃C.

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman and FTIR spectra support the presence of surface -OH groups on the catalysts.
nodes.evidence_snippet: These results were further supported by Raman and Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) spectra (Supporting Information Figure S8, S9).
